title: GS21 baseline with a HUMP-shaped exposure to the priced productivity shock: x loading 1 + (-0.7) (z~^2 - 1)/sqrt2
question: Does a premium hump-shaped in a visible characteristic (productivity, which ROE reveals monotonically) make room and a gap in GS21?
notes:
DIAGNOSIS (2026-10-29, bop_runs/probe/hump_decomp.py). Type EW portfolio returns regressed on the EW market and dy: in vyg25s market beta rises with b, concavely (0.71, 0.87, 1.00, 1.10, 1.19, 1.27) while the residual premium falls (+0.02, +0.10, +0.10, +0.03, -0.07, -0.23 %/mo): two priced channels opposed, with different curvature, sum to the hump. In bvychs both rise with b (beta 0.89 -> 1.19, residual -0.33 -> +0.44). In gvy25s they oppose (market part 0.36 -> 0.26) but the y channel (-0.59 -> +0.71) is ten times the market one, so the sum is monotone.

DESIGN. The direct route to a premium non-monotone in a visible characteristic: firms of middling productivity carry the most aggregate-productivity risk, the most and least productive the least (loading 1.49 at z~ = 0, -0.48 at z~ = +-2). The loading's cross-sectional mean stays 1, so the market keeps its premium. Uses the existing gs_bx2 knob (gvyp10x had +1.0 on top of the product: gap +0.043 against gvyp10's +0.006); the simulator reads gs_bx2 from the solution. Benchmark gsbase (gamma_x 0.5). No y (NY 1).

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-10-29): room 20 to 60% of the linear ceiling, fair gap +0.02 to +0.08, larger at -0.70. Falsified if room stays under 10%: then ROE's rank does not reveal productivity sharply enough, or the premium is not hump-shaped.

method.gs_vy_exposure: no y exposure; x loading 1 + (-0.7) (z~^2 - 1)/sqrt(2), z~ productivity in stationary-sd units

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
